name: JavaScript
description: Fundamental programming language for the web. It's the basis of frontend development and, with Node.js, has also become dominant in the backend.

name: Python
description: High-level, versatile language with clear syntax, extremely popular in web development (Django, Flask), Data Science, Machine Learning, and automation.

name: TypeScript
description: A statically typed superset of the JavaScript language that compiles to plain JavaScript. Essential for large and complex projects.

name: Java
description: Robust, object-oriented language, widely used in enterprise systems, native Android development, and large-scale applications.

name: C#
description: Object-oriented programming language developed by Microsoft as part of the .NET framework, used for web development (ASP.NET), desktop, and games (Unity).

name: SQL
description: The standard language for managing and manipulating relational databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server), indispensable for any application that uses structured data.

name: React
description: A JavaScript library for building component-based user interfaces. The undisputed leader in modern frontend development.

name: Next.js
description: A full-stack React framework that enables Server-Side Rendering (SSR), Static Site Generation (SSG), and easy routing, ideal for scalable and performant React applications.

name: Vue.js
description: A progressive framework for building user interfaces, known for its ease of integration and gentle learning curve.

name: Angular
description: A TypeScript-based platform and framework developed by Google for building large Single-Page Applications (SPAs).

name: Docker
description: Platform that facilitates the creation, deployment, and running of applications using containers, essential in DevOps and modern infrastructure.

name: Kubernetes
description: Open-source system for automating deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications, essential for large-scale orchestration.

name: AWS Lambda
description: Amazon Web Services (AWS) serverless compute service that lets you run code in response to events without managing servers.

name: Git
description: Distributed version control system designed to handle everything from small to very large projects with speed and efficiency. Essential for collaboration.

name: PostgreSQL
description: Robust, open-source object-relational database management system, known for its SQL compliance and extensibility.

name: MongoDB
description: NoSQL document database, known for its flexibility and horizontal scalability, widely used in modern web applications.

name: Terraform
description: Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tool that allows you to declaratively provision and manage cloud resources, essential in cloud environments.

name: Go
description: Statically typed, compiled programming language developed by Google, focused on simplicity, high performance, and concurrency, ideal for microservices.

name: Kotlin
description: Modern, statically typed programming language that runs on the JVM, widely used for Android development and as a modern alternative to Java in the backend.

name: Rust
description: Systems programming language focused on safety, concurrency, and performance.

name: Swift
description: Modern and fast programming language developed by Apple for iOS, macOS, watchOS, and tvOS.

name: Elixir
description: Dynamic, functional programming language based on the Erlang virtual machine (BEAM), ideal for scalable and fault-tolerant systems.

name: Scala
description: Language that combines features of object-oriented and functional programming, running on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM).

name: Clojure
description: A modern, dynamic, and functional Lisp dialect that aims for robustness and concurrency, running on the JVM.

name: Svelte
description: Frontend framework that compiles code into Vanilla JavaScript at build time, resulting in less overhead and better performance.

name: SolidJS
description: Declarative library for creating user interfaces, focused on performance and fine-grained reactivity without the use of a Virtual DOM.

name: Qwik
description: Web framework focused on resumability and instant loading, minimizing the amount of JavaScript that needs to be loaded initially.

name: Phoenix
description: High-performance web framework written in Elixir, known for its robustness and ability to handle millions of simultaneous connections.

name: Django
description: High-level web framework that encourages rapid development and clean, pragmatic design (based on Python).

name: Spring Boot
description: Framework for simplifying the configuration and development of stand-alone applications based on the Spring ecosystem (Java).

name: NestJS
description: Framework for building efficient and scalable server-side applications, based on Node.js and inspired by Angular.

name: Redis
description: In-memory data structure store (key-value) used as a cache, database, and message broker.

name: Cassandra
description: Distributed and highly scalable NoSQL database, designed to handle large amounts of data across clusters of servers.

name: MariaDB
description: Open-source relational database management system, a community fork of MySQL.

name: Helm
description: Package manager for Kubernetes that helps define, install, and upgrade more complex K8s applications.

name: Ansible
description: Open-source automation tool for software provisioning, configuration management, and application deployment.

name: Pulumi
description: Infrastructure as Code platform that allows defining infrastructure using real programming languages (instead of DSLs).

name: WebAssembly
description: Low-level binary instruction format for a stack-based virtual machine, designed to be a high-performance compilation target for the web.

name: Kafka
description: Distributed event streaming platform designed to handle real-time data feeds.

name: RabbitMQ
description: Open-source message broker that implements the Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP).

name: gRPC
description: High-performance, open-source RPC (Remote Procedure Call) framework, developed by Google, using HTTP/2 for transport.

name: FastAPI
description: Modern and fast web framework for building APIs in Python, based on standard typing and asynchronicity.

name: Prometheus
description: Highly scalable open-source monitoring and alerting system, designed for microservices environments.

name: Grafana
description: Open-source visualization and analytics platform, used to create interactive dashboards from various data sources.

name: C
description: General-purpose imperative programming language, known for its efficiency and closeness to hardware, the foundation for many operating systems.

name: PHP
description: Open-source scripting language, widely used for server-side web development and building dynamic applications.

name: Dart
description: Programming language optimized for user interface (UI), created by Google, popularly used with the Flutter framework.

name: Haskell
description: Purely functional and lazy programming language, known for its strong type system and emphasis on immutability.

name: Ruby on Rails
description: MVC (Model-View-Controller) web framework that favors convention over configuration, allowing rapid web application development.

name: Laravel
description: Open-source web framework for PHP, known for its elegant syntax and robust features for building modern applications.

name: .NET
description: Microsoft's open-source development platform for building all types of applications, including web, mobile, and desktop.

name: Express.js
description: Minimalist and flexible framework for Node.js, widely used for building robust APIs and web applications.

name: Gin
description: Web framework written in Go, known for its high performance and simplicity, ideal for building microservices and REST APIs.

name: SQLite
description: Relational database management system that does not require a separate server process, making it ideal for embedded applications and testing.

name: Neo4j
description: Leading NoSQL graph database, optimized for storing and querying highly interconnected data.

name: CockroachDB
description: Distributed, scalable, and fault-tolerant SQL database, designed to survive machine and data center failures.

name: Vault
description: HashiCorp tool for managing secrets and protecting sensitive data, controlling access to tokens, passwords, and cryptographic keys.

name: Jenkins
description: Open-source automation server for CI/CD (Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery), widely used to automate parts of software development.

name: GitLab CI
description: Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery tool natively integrated into the GitLab platform, using YAML files to define pipelines.

name: OpenTofu
description: Open-source fork of the Infrastructure as Code tool Terraform, focused on maintaining an agnostic, community-driven project.

name: Istio
description: An open-source Service Mesh that provides a uniform way to integrate microservices, adding security, routing, and observability.

name: Envoy
description: Open-source service proxy designed for microservices architectures, acting as a universal communication bus.

name: Serverless Framework
description: Framework for developing and deploying serverless architectures on cloud providers, facilitating the management of FaaS functions.

name: Cypress
description: Next-generation frontend testing framework that makes it easy to set up, write, and run end-to-end (E2E) tests on web applications.

name: Jest
description: JavaScript testing framework maintained by Facebook, focused on simplicity and speed, ideal for unit and integration tests.

name: Puppet
description: Configuration management platform that allows defining infrastructure as code and automating system administration.

name: Bazel
description: Open-source build and test tool developed by Google, known for its speed, scalability, and reproducibility.

name: Zero Trust
description: A security model that requires strict verification for every user and device, regardless of network location, following the principle of 'never trust, always verify'.

name: OAuth 2.0
description: Standard authorization protocol that allows an application to obtain limited access to a user's account on an HTTP service without revealing login credentials.
